scene_objective: Ben wakes the three survivors. Sera orients first — disciplined and formal, reaching for command before comfort; Torin second — warm, commanding, steady, counting the dead before himself; Kael last — quiet, watchful, saying nothing yet because silence once kept him alive. Three people a thousand years out of their own time, not three exposition devices.
opening_mode: Ben's hand on the stasis release feels like a choice he can't take back. The first chamber's field dissolves, and a woman with the bearing of a soldier opens eyes that have been closed for a thousand years.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben pulls the stasis release lever — the first chamber's field dissolves with an audible hiss of released pressure
Sera Varik opens her eyes and immediately assumes a combat crouch before orientation hits, then demands identity and chain of command because command language is the only stable ground she has
Torin Hal emerges from the second chamber, staggers, catches himself on the doorframe with one hand, then looks past Ben to count which chambers still hold bodies
Kael Drenn exits the third chamber in silence, back against the wall, scanning the room and cataloguing exits with the discipline of someone taught that speech creates targets
Ben gives the year. Sera absorbs it through rank and duty, Torin through names he will never report back to, and Kael through the blank fact that even the war which owned him is dead

turning_point.trigger: Sera recognises Ben as Jedi-trained but not of her era. 'What year is it?' Ben answers. The room holds its breath. All three register the number differently, and all three begin the private math of wh
turning_point.shift: Sera recognises Ben as Jedi-trained but not of her era. 'What year is it?' Ben answers. The room holds its breath. All three register the number differently, and all three begin the private math of wh

closing_beat: Torin is the last to orient. He looks at the eight dark chambers, the empty one, and says quietly: 'Who got out?'

emotional_arc.shift: Tense anticipation -> the shock of contact across centuries -> growing dread as scope becomes apparent

anti_patterns: Ben should not, in this scene, read Torin's signature as 'something slipping toward dark' or narrate the anchor architecture
Note the three-signature contrast is the chapter's load-bearing image; keep it unhurried and specific, one line apiece, and do not stack metaphors on it
Do not arrive at diagnostic-voice articulation of the Force presences—register them as sensory impressions, not analytical readings
